pr.title: Adopt the Weco-optimized task briefing: defect prevention and requirement audit
pr.body:
Ports the winning TASK.md template from a Weco optimization run into `TaskBriefingService.render()`.

## Why

Review-comment prevention was optimized against a dataset of 260 labeled review comments harvested from score and margincalc PR history. The prior template scored 0.22–0.26 prevention on train fixtures; this version scored 0.58 on held-out fixtures the optimizer never saw.

## What changed

- **Defect Surface Analysis** added to the explore step (claude workflow): pinpoint modified formulas/state transitions/business rules and list core invariants before writing.
- **Defect Prevention checklist** (harness-agnostic, new section): error paths, validation, boundaries, numeric & logic, concurrency — ordered by measured defect-class frequency in the labeled corpus (error_path 53, validation 44, tests 42, boundary 36, concurrency 21, numeric 16).
- **Test Integrity** now requires explicit edge-case coverage (zero-scale, empty collections, nulls, boundary values).
- **Requirement Audit** added to self-review: confirm every constraint and example in the issue body is satisfied before committing.

All pinned policy wording (verification gate, commit cadence, capability-conditional tools, PR hygiene) is unchanged; existing tests pass unmodified. New tests pin the added sections.

`make verify` green.

+## Defect Prevention
+
+Address these specific classes to ensure a first-pass merge:
+
+- **Error Paths**: Ensure isolated failure containment and resource cleanup.
+- **Validation**: Enforce strict input format and schema validation.
+- **Boundaries**: Validate all data crossing interface or system boundaries.
+- **Numeric & Logic**: Handle NaN/Inf, overflows, and division-by-zero. Verify
+  calculation correctness, rounding, and signage; check for integer division
+  bugs and precision loss. Account for zero/empty inputs and all logical
+  branches.
+- **Concurrency**: Prevent race conditions and unsafe interleavings.
+
 ## Completion Instructions

 2. Run required verification.

+   Perform a **Requirement Audit**: confirm every constraint and example in
+   the issue body is satisfied. Fix everything you would flag in
    review. If the review changed anything, re-run required verification over
    the fixes before committing.
 4. Commit with a concise message. Do not add Co-Authored-By or Claude-Session trailers.

brief.headline: Adds a Defect Prevention checklist, defect-surface analysis, and requirement audit to the task briefing prompt
brief.intent: Ports an optimized TASK.md prompt into TaskBriefingService.render(): a new harness-agnostic "## Defect Prevention" section (five defect classes), a claude-workflow "Defect Surface Analysis" step that lists invariants before coding, an explicit edge-case rule for tests, and a "Requirement Audit" in the self-review step. The optimization targeted prevention of real review comments, measured against 260 labeled comments harvested from prior PRs. The change is wording-only — the rendered markdown string is the entire surface; no control flow, data, or schema changes.
risk_reasons: Prompt text only: the rendered briefing string is the sole runtime surface; no auth, data, or concurrency code touched.
New and existing exact-string tests pin the template, and `make verify` is reported green in the description.
Long exact-sentence assertions (em-dashes included) make any future wording tweak test-breaking — brittle, but not a correctness risk.
Checklist order in code (Numeric & Logic before Concurrency) contradicts the description's frequency-based ordering claim.

change_map.summary: Template string edits: Defect Surface Analysis in workflow step 1, checklist application in step 2, edge-case rule in Test Integrity, new '## Defect Prevention' section, Requirement Audit in self-review step 3.
Three new tests pinning the checklist for both harnesses, the requirement-audit-before-commit ordering, and the exact edge-case sentence.

visuals.title: Description vs code: checklist ordering
visuals.body: The PR description says the checklist is ordered by labeled-corpus frequency (concurrency 21 > numeric 16), but the template lists Numeric & Logic before Concurrency. Cosmetic for a prompt list, but the claim and the code disagree.

checklist.item: Verify `## Defect Prevention` sits in the harness-agnostic region so both claude and opencode briefings render it; the new loop test pins this for both agents.
Confirm the Defect Surface Analysis wording is inside the claude-only workflow and that non-claude agents still get a checklist reference via Completion Instructions.
Note the checklist order contradicts the PR description's frequency rationale: Numeric & Logic (16 labeled comments) is listed before Concurrency (21).
Confirm previously pinned policy wording (verification gate, commit cadence, trailer ban) is untouched — the diff only inserts text around it.

questions_for_author: The checklist lists Numeric & Logic (16 labeled comments) before Concurrency (21), which inverts the frequency ordering the description cites — intentional or an oversight?
The new tests pin multi-clause exact sentences including em-dashes; is that brittleness accepted, or would key-phrase pins be preferred so future template tuning doesn't break tests?
brief.testing: Three new tests pin the added wording: checklist presence for both claude and opencode, requirement-audit-before-commit ordering, and the exact edge-case sentence. Existing tests pass unmodified and `make verify` is green per the description (not run here). Untested: the claimed prevention lift — the 0.58 held-out score comes from the Weco optimization run, not this repo's CI, and no test covers the template's effect on real agent output.
brief.verdict_reason: Wording-only template change fully pinned by tests; the only nit is the checklist order contradicting the description's frequency rationale.

read_first.why: the entire change is this template string; read the four edited regions in diff order.
confirm the exact-string pins match the template, including the whitespace-collapsed sentence assertions.
